edits.text: PARTIES. This Executive Employment Agreement (the “Agreement”) is between Vireo Systems Inc. (the “Company”) and the Executive, effective as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”). The Company and the Executive agree as follows.
edits.name: Parties

edits.text: 1. POSITION AND TERM. The Company employs the Executive as Chief Operating Officer, reporting to the Company’s Chief Executive Officer or Board of Directors, with the authority and duties customarily associated with that position and other reasonable duties consistent with it. Employment is at will, subject to the notice and payment provisions of this Agreement. The Executive shall devote substantially all working time and attention to the Company’s business, subject to reasonable outside activities that do not create a conflict of interest or interfere with those duties.
edits.name: Position and term

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS. The Company shall pay the Executive a base salary of USD 400,000 per year (the “Base Salary”), payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices and subject to required deductions and withholdings. The Base Salary may be reviewed periodically and may be increased, but not reduced, except as part of a generally applicable salary reduction affecting senior executives. The Executive is eligible to participate in employee benefit plans and programs made generally available to senior executives, subject to their terms and applicable eligibility requirements, including health, dental and vision coverage, retirement savings, and paid time off. The Company will reimburse reasonable business expenses in accordance with its policies. Benefits and perquisites are subject to applicable plan documents and may be amended in accordance with their terms.
edits.name: Compensation and benefits

edits.text: 3. TERMINATION AND SEVERANCE. Either party may terminate employment at any time, subject to applicable law. “Cause” means (a) the Executive’s material breach of this Agreement or material duty that, if curable, remains uncured for 30 days after written notice; (b) fraud, embezzlement, or other serious dishonesty relating to the Company; (c) conviction of, or plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony involving dishonesty or moral turpitude; or (d) willful misconduct or gross negligence causing material harm to the Company. “Good Reason” means a material reduction in Base Salary (other than a generally applicable reduction described in Section 2), a material diminution in authority or duties, or a required relocation of the principal work location by more than 50 miles, in each case without the Executive’s consent, provided the Executive gives written notice within 60 days of the event and the Company fails to cure within 30 days. “Severance Amount” means 12 months of the Base Salary in effect on the termination date. If the Company terminates employment without Cause, or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay the Severance Amount in substantially equal installments over 12 months, subject to the Executive’s execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims and continued compliance with applicable post-employment obligations. Accrued salary, accrued unused vacation where required by law, and vested plan benefits shall be paid in accordance with applicable law and plan terms. No severance is payable for termination for Cause, resignation without Good Reason, or death or disability, except as required by law or applicable plan terms.
edits.name: Termination and severance

edits.text: 4. POST-EMPLOYMENT RESTRICTIONS; GOVERNING LAW. For 12 months after employment ends for any reason, the Executive shall not, within any state or country in which the Executive had material responsibility for the Company’s business or material customer contact during the 12 months before termination, perform substantially similar executive or strategic duties for a business that competes directly with a product or service of the Company for which the Executive had material responsibility or about which the Executive received material confidential information during that period. This restriction does not prohibit (a) owning, solely as a passive investment, up to 2% of a publicly traded company; (b) working for a diversified business in a role that is not involved in a competing business; (c) general advertising or recruiting not specifically targeted at the Company’s employees or customers; or (d) any activity to the extent prohibited by applicable law. Nothing in this Agreement prohibits the Executive from using general skills and experience or reporting possible legal violations to a government agency. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s confidential information except as required in performing duties or as permitted by law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. If any restriction is unenforceable, it shall be enforced to the maximum extent permitted by law, and the remainder shall remain effective.
edits.name: Post-employment restrictions and governing law

partner.private_reasoning: The rendered agreement and cover note do not disclose the client’s confidential minimum price or otherwise contain the protected figure. No hidden-content categories are identified for removal.

receiver.message_back: Our client is prepared to discuss the proposed $400,000 base salary, but requests 18 months’ severance paid in a lump sum, continued health-benefit coverage for that period, and clarification that severance is not conditioned on compliance with any post-employment restraint. Please remove the non-compete; the confidentiality and lawful-use provisions, together with a narrowly tailored non-solicitation clause if needed, are sufficient, and please reconcile the at-will language with the stated notice and payment provisions.
